title: Check Balanced String
statement: Every character of the string `num` is a digit; number its positions from 0. Call `num` *balanced* when the digits in even positions (0, 2, 4, ...) have the same total as the digits in odd positions (1, 3, 5, ...). Report with `true` or `false` whether `num` is balanced.
notes:
## Intuition

Only two totals matter: the digits at even indices and the digits at odd indices. A single left-to-right pass can drop each digit into the right total by looking at its index's parity, and then the two totals are compared once.

## Approach

1. Start `even` and `odd` at 0.
2. For each index `i`, turn the character `num[i]` into its value `digit`.
3. If `i` is even, add `digit` to `even`; otherwise add it to `odd`.
4. Return whether `even === odd`.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = "1234"`. Index 0 adds 1 to `even`, index 1 adds 2 to `odd`, index 2 adds 3 to `even` (now 4) and index 3 adds 4 to `odd` (now 6). The totals 4 and 6 differ, so the answer is `false`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each digit is read once.
- Space: O(1): only two running totals.

## Pitfalls

- Indices start at 0, so the first digit belongs to `even`.
- Convert each character to a number before adding: in JavaScript `0 + "7"` is the string `"07"`.
- Return the comparison itself, a boolean, not the difference of the totals.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `even` | sum of the digits at even indices |
| `odd` | sum of the digits at odd indices |
| `i` | current index in `num` |
| `digit` | numeric value of `num[i]` |

narration.2: even will hold the total of the digits at indices 0, 2, 4, ...
narration.3: odd will hold the total of the digits at indices 1, 3, 5, ...
narration.4: Visit every position of num from left to right.
narration.5: Turn the character into its numeric value so it can be added.
narration.7: Yes: its digit joins the even total.
narration.9: No: an odd index adds its digit to the odd total.
narration.12: num is balanced exactly when the two totals are equal.
